title: Continuous mathematics in iPRA: claim and verification status
scope: Major mathematical claims and their separate human, host-Lean, implementation-example, and object-iPRA verification layers. This is not an exhaustive independent audit of every upstream theorem.

baseline.upstream_status: Targeted source inspection; upstream object-iPRA modules were not rebuilt in this session.

status_vocabulary.human_argument.provided: A developed human-readable mathematical proof is in the referenced report section under its stated hypotheses. This is not machine certification.
status_vocabulary.kernel_checked: The stated finite or metric host-Lean theorem has been accepted by the pinned Lean kernel; its exact scope is given per claim.
status_vocabulary.partially_kernel_checked: A precisely identified portion is checked; the broader claim remains a human argument.
status_vocabulary.supporting_kernel_only: A general supporting arithmetic lemma is checked, but the displayed claim has not itself been formalized.
status_vocabulary.typed_targets_only: Definitions and proposition types compile; the proposition has not been proved. A Goal definition does not assert its inhabitance.
status_vocabulary.uncompiled_outline_only: The Lean-looking blueprint is excluded from the checked build and carries no typechecking claim.
status_vocabulary.not_formalized_as_a_theorem: No direct Lean proof of this claim is delivered.
status_vocabulary.finite_examples_passed: Exact finite reference calculations passed; they are not universal proofs.
status_vocabulary.new_derivation_not_delivered: No new theorem of type Prf PRAAx for this claim has been constructed in this package.

checked_host_lean.constructivity_boundary: Classical.choice occurs in the actual host proof dependency audit. The host result is not by itself an intuitionistic object-language derivation or a proof-producing translation.

object_ipra_summary.status: Explicit arithmetic formulas, finite invariants, and a source-aware implementation route are supplied; endpoint construction remains.
required_method: Keep each input evaluator/modulus as a fixed PR definition with proved numerical contracts, or use a bounded evaluator with an explicit PR clock.
Use natural-number and signed-rational codes with guarded lengths and positive denominators.
Represent finite universal input checks by primitive-recursive Boolean conjunction folds.
Carry the specified quantifier-free prefix invariants through induction; no induction on arbitrary quantified formulas is assumed.
Build concrete Prf PRAAx derivation terms through the existing arithmetic and proof-producing backend.
Keep semantic completions and host Lean theorems distinct from those derivation terms.

claims.title: Uniform integrability plus a rho-Cauchy rate constructs an L1 limit
hypotheses: Jointly PR regular L1 names S(n,j).
Monotone PR cutoffs U(k)>=1 with Tail_U(k)(f_n)<=2^-k uniformly in n.
A monotone PR rho-Cauchy rate R.
claims.result: q(k)=k+2+ceilLog2(2U(k+2)) and N(k)=R(q(k)) give an L1 Cauchy rate; b_k=S(N(k+2),k+2) is the output regular name. Its integrability and inherited tail control are conclusions.

claims.title: Counterexamples delimit the effective interface
hypotheses: The explicit finite, probability, and machine-simulation examples described in the report.
claims.result: The report proves the need for norm-specific contracts and supplied or derived rates: bounded/UI martingales have no uniform computable Cauchy-rate extractor; conditional projections need not converge in operator norm; L1 error does not control suprema; atomless event algebras are not compact; small differential changes can change homology.

remaining: No positive object-iPRA derivation is claimed for conclusions refuted by these counterexamples.

limitations: The halting argument is an external computability limitation, not a claim that iPRA internally proves its own general soundness.

not_claimed: A completed new embedding of unrestricted real/complex analysis, category theory, or model theory into iPRA.
A total primitive-recursive universal evaluator for all primitive-recursive programs.
Automatic construction of missing tail, Cauchy, compactness, mass-margin, operator, or local-model data from qualitative existence assertions.
A Lean proof of the complete Vitali lifting theorem, integrated formula evaluator, complex-analysis extension, or HPL theorem.
Rebuilding or exhaustively verifying the pinned upstream repository.
Replacing the existing valid common-dominator truncation theorem by a counterexample.
Universal correctness inferred from the Python examples.
Optimal error scheduling, polynomial-time complexity, or a uniform speed improvement for every application.
